uncertainty: Sixteen distinct Java package input paths passed the valid ASCII PLY control; they include native readers and bindings that share parser engines. Seven pinned open-source Maven package paths, jPLY 0.2.0, MeshIO 2.1.2, mesh-ply 1.1.0, pcutil 0.3.0, LWJGL Assimp 3.4.3, MonkeyWrench 1.0.1, and JavaGL Ply 0.0.4, parsed the valid ASCII PLY triangle and returned three vertices, one face and face indices [0,1,2]. Source-built F3D 4.0.1 separately returned one actor, three parsed points and one cell. Four more verified paths are needed for the 20-path working target. Four bounded Maven Central searches saved seven unique name hits; some queries timed out and successful snapshots were retained across refreshes. Search names are not parser proof; MeshIO, pcutil and MonkeyWrench came from project documentation. The Ardor3D PLY importer remains an unresolved lead. ArtiSynth Maspack PlyReader is another lead: its official 3.9 ZIP and local API passed a temporary control run, but the distribution includes noncommercial TetGen and a separately released BSD-only reader package is not established, so it is not included. Only a triangle with float vertices and one face was demonstrated; other PLY properties and binary PLY are untested. No malformed-input, resource-use, or vulnerability experiments were run. The source build used LLVM 23.1.4 with the optional C and Java bindings; C++20 algorithm and vector headers were preincluded for the recorded host toolchain. There is no Maven artifact or comparable deps.dev exact-release metric for this source-built binding, so it is unranked; the F3D Homebrew count is not mixed into the Java ranking.
